To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated a plasmonic dye-sensitized photoanode that shows an efficiency of 22% higher than that of a conventional photoanode and 49% higher than that without a blocking layer.
the incorporation of plasmonic Ag nanoparticles into the porous Nb2O5 film, which is used as a blocking layer, enhances the efficiency of the cell by 22%.

a simple, one-step process for the fabrication of a plasmon-enhanced dye-sensitized photoanode is demonstrated and that it leads to the enhancement of the power conversion efficiency by 22% when compared with its non-plasmonic counterpart.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an inexpensive and simple strategy for the incorporation of plasmonic metal nanoparticles into a blocking layer, which can be used in DSSCs for the enhancement of the efficiency.
the synthesis of a plasmonically active blocking layer that can be easily integrated into a dye-sensitizer solar cell.
the development of a simple and cost-effective method of fabricating a plasmonic dye-sensitized photoanode with a plasmonic metal blocking layer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a plasmonic-blocking-layer is a promising strategy for enhancing the efficiency of DSSC.
the present study demonstrates the potential of plasmonic blocking layers in DSSCs, which could be a cost-effective and viable alternative for conventional plasmonic nanostructure-based DSSCs.
the plasmonic effect is a very important parameter that should be considered in the design and development of plasmonic solar cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plasmonic metal nanoparticles can be used as an efficient light-harvesting layer and as an electron-blocking layer, which can be achieved by a simple one-pot synthesis.
a plasmonic layer can be used for the fabrication of efficient DSSC without any additional steps and at a low cost.

we have demonstrated that a simple one-step method can be used to integrate plasmonic nanoparticles into the porous structure, which can be used as a plasmonic light harvesting layer in dye-sensitized photovoltaics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple one-step synthesis of plasmon-enhanced DSSCs is possible, which is a step toward the realization of plasmonic DSSCs.
the concept of a blocking layer can be used for the integration of plasmonic nanostructures into the porous structure without any additional cost or complexity.
plasmonic nanoparticles can be incorporated into the porous photoanode by a simple one-pot process, and their effect on the performance of DSSC can be studied in the absence of other additives.
